title: `migrate` from gcs backend is broken (context canceled / timeout)
body:
**Describe the bug**

When trying to migrate from GCS backend to some other backend (raft initially, but same issue happens with file), the migration process fails with `context canceled` after some time. When using the following configuration file :
```
storage_source "gcs" {
  bucket = "test-vault-migation"
}

storage_destination "file" {
  path    = "data"
}
cluster_addr = "http://127.0.0.1:8201"
```

on a VM with enough CPU/RAM/disk, located in same region than bucket, the first migration run will fail after ~37.5k items synced (this is consistent over time / retry, they all fail between 37.5k and 37.6k). 

If I then start again using the `-start` option with the last item synced, process will be stuck at `[DEBUG] creating client` for around 4m20s and then fail with : `Error migrating: failed to scan for children: failed to read object: context canceled`.

What is already synced / available at destination doesn't matter, I can empty my `data` dir and will still get the same issue.

This is, right now, blocking our production system.

**Expected behavior**
Migration process should work flawlessly

**Environment:**
* Vault CLI Version (retrieve with `vault version`): v1.41.1
* Server Operating System/Architecture: debian 12

Vault server configuration file(s):

```hcl
storage_source "gcs" {
  bucket = "test-vault-migation"
}

storage_destination "file" {
  path    = "data"
}
cluster_addr = "http://127.0.0.1:8201"
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hello... continuing the conversation from https://<redacted-host>/t/vault-operator-migrate-keeps-failing-with-context-canceled/57382, and given what you've said above, to me it sounds highly likely that this is a data dependent issue that will only reproduce using your particular Vault data in GCS, or other data of similar shape and size.


Vault expects all its storage backends to be able to list all the keys under a prefix up to the next slash character, and this operation is sometimes a bad fit (expensive to perform) for some backends.

I have a hunch that you have a very large number of keys in a particular "directory" of storage, and fetching the complete list from GCS is timing out.

Are you able to identify which "directory" is being listed when the operation times out, and share the path?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Glad you got to the bottom of it in the end! This has clearly exposed a severe lack of surfacing appropriate error messages.

About your last sentence though...

> migration does not convert data based on the limit of each backend :(

there is no conversion it could realistically do ... Vault doesn't have an abstraction layer to allow for larger data to be packed into backends that can't cope with it. Unfortunately your way forward appears to now require finding and deleting the large data stored within this KVv2 secrets engine.

**------------------- UPDATE AFTER FEW MINS ------------------**
I fixed the issue by creating the tables in destination storage(postgresql) from [here](https://<redacted-host>/vault/docs/configuration/storage/postgresql)

[Migration docs](https://<redacted-host>/vault/docs/commands/operator/migrate) bit confusing for me, saying

> Keys in the destination storage backend will be overwritten, **_and the destination should not be initialized prior to the migrate operation._**

It would be nice improve documentation what does "initialized" means
